title: P0 prod regression: v8.3.10.2 shell.js breaks play button (rolled back via hot-patch)
description:
Bosco reported 2026-05-03 ~11:30 CDT that the play button no longer works when clicking from the grid or My Library on prod after v8.3.10.2 deploy. Hot-patched prod by reverting /opt/audiobooks/library/web-v2/js/shell.js to the v8.3.10.1 version (sha1 4df270fae9acedaf64cd60b63822a4a1262a5c5c). Bumped cachebust to 1777826705 across 13 web-v2 files. The broken v8.3.10.2 shell.js (sha1 6019b9e29cd7c88a79038d503531f9cf06dfdf13) was preserved at /opt/audiobooks/library/web-v2/js/shell.js.broken-8.3.10.2 for forensic analysis. The new /api/audiobooks/<id>/chapters endpoint (issue 7bf, server-side) is left in place — it still works correctly (verified returning 74 chapters for Water Mirror Echo), so the regression is purely client-side in shell.js.

**Diff to investigate** (git diff v8.3.10.1 v8.3.10.2 -- library/web-v2/js/shell.js): adds  reset, ,  call at line 463, non-blocking chapters fetch at line 471, and the  helper method at line 696. None of these jump out as a play-blocker on static analysis — fetch is non-blocking,  guards prevent null-deref. **Need browser-based reproduction** on devlib.thebosco.club (which still has v8.3.10.2 shell.js) to capture the actual JS console error or audio.play() rejection reason.

**Hypotheses to investigate**:
1. Cross-frame user-gesture activation lost due to the new fetch() invocation between book-load and audio.play() (line 545-547 comment explicitly warns about this pattern)
2. _applyChapterButtonVisibility called pre-DOM-ready in some new code path
3. An unhandled promise rejection in the chapters fetch chain that propagates to break the surrounding async playBook
4. Some interaction with the streaming-translate.js initialization that wasn't there before

**Required for v8.3.10.3 fix**:
- Identify root cause via browser console capture
- Restore the chapter-skip-buttons-everywhere feature (issue 6ub) without breaking play
- Add a regression test that exercises the play() flow end-to-end (not just structural assertions)
- Roll into v8.3.10.3 staged release
close_reason: Closed

title: Rotate RunPod + Vast.ai credentials exposed in session transcript; verify Vast workergroup 27636 / endpoint 21112 torn down
description:
On 2026-08-26 a read of /etc/audiobooks/audiobooks.conf was piped through ~/.claude/bin/secret-mask, but the masker did not recognise either format and both values printed into an assistant session transcript:

  - AUDIOBOOKS_RUNPOD_API_KEY  (rpa_-prefixed token, was line 94)
  - AUDIOBOOKS_VASTAI_SERVERLESS_API_KEY  (bare 64-char hex, was commented line 102)

Both have since been REMOVED from the config file (see Audiobook-Manager-6ap), but removal is not revocation. The values still authenticate until rotated in the vendor consoles.

RISK ASSESSMENT: the RunPod key is low-value (its endpoints are decommissioned and return 404) but is still an account-scoped credential. The Vast.ai key is the higher risk - that account holds live credit and the key was never disabled upstream, only commented out locally.

SECOND FINDING, from the same config comment block: a Vast.ai serverless workergroup (27636) and endpoint (21112) were provisioned 2026-04-24 and the config carried the note 'Teardown once backlog drains'. They were never enabled on this host and nothing references them. If they still exist in the Vast.ai account they may be billing silently against the credit.

TOOLING GAP (worth fixing separately): secret-mask passed an rpa_-prefixed token and a bare 64-char hex string untouched. Both are common credential shapes.
acceptance_criteria: 1. RunPod API key rotated or revoked in the RunPod console. 2. Vast.ai API key rotated or revoked in the Vast.ai console. 3. Vast.ai workergroup 27636 and endpoint 21112 confirmed either absent or explicitly destroyed, with the console state cited. 4. ~/.claude/bin/secret-mask updated to catch rpa_* tokens and bare 32/64-char hex strings, verified by feeding it both shapes and observing masking.
notes:
=== 2026-08-26 TRIAGE — SCOPE REDUCED TO ONE KEY ===

WHEN: the exposure happened TODAY, ~11:56 CDT, in this session, caused by an
assistant grep of the system config piped through the masking helper. It is not
a pre-existing leak. The operator correctly remembered a Vast.ai rotation on
2026-08-03; that rotation is why half of this issue is already moot.

VALIDITY TESTED (live API, read-only, values never printed):
  Vast.ai   -> GET console.vast.ai/api/v0/users/current/  HTTP 401  DEAD
              (the leaked value is the 2026-04-24 config entry, killed by the
               2026-08-03 rotation — no action needed)
  RunPod    -> GET rest.runpod.io/v1/endpoints            HTTP 200  *** LIVE ***

REMAINING WORK — TWO ITEMS ONLY:
  1. Rotate/revoke the RunPod API key. It authenticates right now. Its serverless
     endpoints are decommissioned so the blast radius is account-level rather
     than workload-level, but it is a live account credential in a transcript.
  2. Confirm Vast.ai workergroup 27636 / endpoint 21112 are torn down. Provisioned
     2026-04-24, never enabled on this host, referenced by no config. Console
     login required (the stored key is dead, so this cannot be checked by API).

TOOLING GAP — WORSE THAN FIRST RECORDED. ~/.claude/secret-exposure.log has NO
entry for the 11:56 command that actually leaked both keys, but DOES have entries
at 12:51:32 and 12:59:36 for two false positives (lines of the form
NAME_FILE=<filesystem path>, which carry no secret). So the masker AND the
post-hoc detector are both blind to rpa_-prefixed tokens and to bare 64-char hex,
while the detector fires on benign pointer declarations. Net effect: the one real
exposure of the day went unlogged and two non-events were logged. Fixing this is
a change to the operator's hook tooling, not to this project — recorded here so
it is not lost.
close_reason:
Both exposed credentials confirmed REVOKED 2026-08-26.

PROOF (live API, read-only, values never printed):
  RunPod  GET rest.runpod.io/v1/endpoints            200 -> 401 (3 consecutive retests)
  Vast.ai GET console.vast.ai/api/v0/users/current/  401 (revoked by the operator's
          2026-08-03 rotation; the leaked value was the 2026-04-24 config entry)

WORTH RECORDING: the operator's first rotation attempt did NOT revoke the RunPod
key — it still returned 200 on three retests afterwards, because RunPod permits
concurrent keys and adding a replacement leaves the old one valid. It went 401
only after an explicit delete. This is precisely the trap Audiobook-Manager-aiq
warns about in its own first work item ('delete the old one, do not just add a
new one'), and it is why 'I rotated it' was verified rather than taken at face
value. A rotation is not a revocation until the old credential is observed
failing.

CONSEQUENCE: the copies of the RunPod key remaining in /root/audiobooks-conf-backups/
and in the /etc/audiobooks/*.bak files are now inert.

SPLIT OUT, NOT DROPPED: this issue's second item — confirming Vast.ai workergroup
27636 / endpoint 21112 are torn down — was not addressed and is carried forward
under its own issue rather than being closed silently.

title: upgrade.sh _require_sudo probes with 'sudo -v', a false negative under NOPASSWD
description: _require_sudo() gated privileged operations on 'sudo -v'. With no controlling TTY the script's sudo wrapper adds -n, so the probe becomes 'sudo -n -v'. That does not ask whether a command can run as root - it asks sudo to validate and refresh the invoking user's auth timestamp, which modern sudo refuses non-interactively even for NOPASSWD: ALL because there is no password to cache. Measured on cachyos-bosco as bosco (NOPASSWD: ALL): 'sudo -n -v' -> 'sudo: a password is required', exit 1, while 'sudo -n true' succeeds. Every privileged call in the script would have worked. The false negative aborted the 8.4.2.2 production upgrade after the backup step and printed guidance blaming the missing TTY, which sent a prior session to an interactive shell to fix a problem that did not exist. The remote deploy path was never affected because it already probes with 'sudo -n true' over ssh - which is why dev and qa deployed cleanly and only local prod blocked.
design: Probe with 'sudo true' - the capability the script actually uses - making the local path agree with the remote path's existing probe.
acceptance_criteria: Under NOPASSWD with no TTY the probe passes; as an account that genuinely cannot escalate (nobody) it still fails; local prod upgrade completes non-interactively.
close_reason: Fixed in v8.4.2.3. Probe changed from 'sudo -v' to 'sudo true'. Verified: under NOPASSWD with no TTY the old probe returns 'a password is required' and the new one passes; run as nobody (genuinely cannot escalate) the new probe still fails. Production upgrade 8.4.2.0 -> 8.4.2.3 then completed non-interactively.

title: Dependabot auto-merge landed 16 commits on main with CI red
description: Branch protection on main had required_status_checks enabled with an EMPTY context list, so gh pr merge --auto in dependabot-auto-merge.yml merged each Dependabot PR the instant it was approved, regardless of CI. Between 2026-08-11 and 2026-08-25 sixteen commits landed that way with CI failing. One of them (#132, mando >=0.8.2,<0.9) conflicts with radon 6.0.1's mando<0.8 ceiling and made requirements-dev.txt unresolvable, so Type Checking, Dependency Vulnerabilities and Python Tests could not run at all for two weeks. Compounding it: GitHub does not start workflow runs for pushes made with GITHUB_TOKEN, so ci.yml's push:main trigger never fired after an auto-merge and the last CI run on main stayed pinned to the 2026-08-06 release commit. Only CodeQL and Dependency Graph ran on main and both were green throughout, so the branch looked healthy. Detected only because python-security.yml has a weekly schedule, which went red 2026-08-17 and 2026-08-24.
design: Three-part fix: (1) 12 required status checks on main with strict:true so auto-merge cannot merge red; (2) daily schedule + workflow_dispatch on ci.yml and security-checks.yml so main is re-validated by a path GITHUB_TOKEN cannot suppress; (3) restore mando>=0.7.1,<0.8 plus a dependabot.yml ignore for mando>=0.8. Also removed required_pull_request_reviews (count 0, approved nothing, emitted Bypassed rule violations on every push) per the solo-repo rule in ~/.claude/rules/github.md.
acceptance_criteria: CI, Python Security & Quality and Security Checks all green on main; required context list verified to match actual check-run names so no PR can hang on a context no workflow produces.
close_reason: Fixed and verified on main 3170685d: CI, Python Security & Quality and Security Checks all green. 12 required status checks live on main (strict), required-context list cross-checked against actual check-run names (zero mismatches). Daily schedule + workflow_dispatch added to ci.yml and security-checks.yml. mando restored to >=0.7.1,<0.8 with a dependabot.yml ignore for >=0.8. jq -> 1.7.1-6+deb13u3, openssl -> 3.5.7-1~deb13u2, apt layer build-verified against the FROM digest.

title: upgrade.sh rsync --delete never purges already-leaked dev artifacts: --exclude patterns also protect existing target files from deletion
description:
Discovered during Phase 10a staged-release VM testing of v8.4.2.0 on
test-audiobook-cachyos, while verifying the HIGH-1 leak fix
(_NEVER_SHIP_EXCLUDES in upgrade.sh, CHANGELOG entry re:
.claude-session-ring.jsonl reaching /opt/audiobooks/library/web-v2/ and
becoming fetchable over HTTPS).

HTTP-level verification PASSES: curl to
https://<vm>:8090/.claude-session-ring.jsonl,
https://<vm>:8090/css/.claude-session-ring.jsonl and
https://<vm>:8090/proxy_server.py all return 404 (the
_is_forbidden_static_path dot-file deny-list in proxy_server.py::_serve_static
correctly blocks them).

But the files are still PHYSICALLY PRESENT on disk on this VM:
  /opt/audiobooks/library/web-v2/.claude-session-ring.jsonl
  /opt/audiobooks/library/web-v2/css/.claude-session-ring.jsonl
(stat shows Birth/Modify = 2026-05-23, i.e. from the VM's original install,
predating this v8.4.2.0 deploy -- confirmed NOT freshly reintroduced by
today's rsync).

Root cause: upgrade.sh's library sync (~line 1846) runs
  rsync -av --delete "${_NEVER_SHIP_EXCLUDES[@]}" ... "$project/library/" "$target/library/"
_NEVER_SHIP_EXCLUDES includes --exclude='.claude*' and --exclude='SESSION_RECORD*'.
Per rsync semantics, --delete does NOT remove files on the receiver that match
an --exclude pattern unless --delete-excluded is also passed. So a file
matching .claude* that ever lands in $target once (e.g. from an install
predating this fix, or any other pre-fix code path) is now PERMANENTLY
protected from cleanup by every future upgrade -- the same pattern that
stops new leaks also shields old ones from ever being removed.

This is NOT a fresh regression (fresh syncs correctly exclude these files --
confirmed via test_upgrade_never_ship_excludes.py and this VM's version now
correctly reads 8.4.2.0), and the static-serving deny-list currently blocks
HTTP access, so there is no active exposure on this VM right now. But:
 - Any other install whose /opt/audiobooks predates the exclude fix (e.g. the
   real production host, or any QA mirror) could be carrying the same
   never-cleaned files, invisible to every future upgrade.sh run.
 - The mitigation is single-layered in practice for these old copies: it
   depends entirely on the static-file deny-list never regressing. A future
   change to _is_forbidden_static_path (or an alternate serving path that
   doesn't go through it) would make a 2.5-month-old session transcript
   fetchable again with zero further code changes needed.

NOT a safe fix: blindly adding --delete-excluded to the existing rsync would
also delete `venv`, `certs`, `audiobooks.db`, `testdata` -- all in the same
_NEVER_SHIP_EXCLUDES-adjacent exclude lists and REQUIRED to persist on the
target. Any fix needs to distinguish "never allowed to exist on target,
purge on sight" (the _NEVER_SHIP_EXCLUDES set) from "exists on target
intentionally, never touch" (venv/certs/db/testdata) -- these are currently
handled by the same blanket --exclude mechanism and need to diverge.

Suggested fix: add a dedicated purge step in upgrade.sh's library-sync path
that explicitly find-deletes _NEVER_SHIP_EXCLUDES-pattern files already
present under $target (dev artifacts only -- never venv/certs/db/testdata),
run unconditionally on every upgrade regardless of whether the source tree
currently contains them.

Also found in passing and already cleaned up (not committed, not shipped --
gitignored untracked files, not a release blocker): the *project's own*
working tree had two stale copies of the same artifact,
library/web-v2/.claude-session-ring.jsonl and
library/web-v2/css/.claude-session-ring.jsonl (mtimes 2026-07-28 / 2026-04-27),
apparently left over from whenever this bug was originally reproduced
locally. Deleted during this test session.
close_reason: Fixed in staged v8.4.2.0 (commit 6702c4de) and PROVEN end-to-end on test-audiobook-cachyos: a real --remote deploy 8.4.0.1->8.4.2.0 WITHOUT --force completed EXIT 0 (90x); 'Purged 383 leaked dev artifact(s)' removed seeded .claude-session-ring.jsonl + stale.py.backup while venv survived, leaked path 404 over HTTPS (emq/qlr); smoke probe reported '1 warning(s), 0 failures' with the credential-less downloader downgraded to a warning (bqe). 32 new regression tests; full suite 5356 passed.

title: upgrade.sh --remote never generates a preflight report, so every remote deploy fails without --force
description:
Discovered during Phase 10a staged-release VM testing of v8.4.2.0 (test-audiobook-cachyos).

do_remote_upgrade() (upgrade.sh ~line 308) rsyncs the project to a fresh
/tmp/audiobook-upgrade-$$ directory on the remote host and invokes:
  sudo -n '$remote_tmp/upgrade.sh' --from-project '$remote_tmp' --target '$remote_target' --yes

It never calls --check first (which would run generate_preflight and write
${AUDIOBOOKS_VAR_DIR}/.control/upgrade-preflight.json on the remote), and it
never passes --force. The remote-side upgrade.sh then hits validate_preflight()
(line ~1678), finds no preflight file, prints "Preflight check required before
upgrade." and exits 1 — every single time, for every --remote invocation,
because each remote run uses a brand-new random temp dir as PROJECT_DIR so
even a manually pre-generated preflight report's recorded "source" field
would never match on a subsequent run.

Reproduced live:
  ./upgrade.sh --from-project . --remote 192.168.122.104 --user claude \
      --ssh-key ~/.claude/ssh/id_ed25519 --yes
  -> "Preflight check required before upgrade." / exit 1

Impact: --remote is the documented, intended path for deploying to QA/test
VMs (vm-test-manifest.json test_environments, project-vm-map.json
deploy_script=./upgrade.sh). It is currently unusable without --force, which
bypasses the LEAPP-inspired drift-detection preflight system entirely --
defeating the safety feature for the one pathway (unattended remote deploy)
that would benefit from it most.

Suggested fix: do_remote_upgrade should either (a) run the remote upgrade.sh
twice in the same remote temp dir -- once with --check, once for real -- so
the preflight source path matches, or (b) pass --force explicitly and treat
that as an accepted tradeoff for the remote/CI deploy path, documented as such.

Workaround used for this test run: --force (script's own suggested tip).
close_reason: Fixed in staged v8.4.2.0 (commit 6702c4de) and PROVEN end-to-end on test-audiobook-cachyos: a real --remote deploy 8.4.0.1->8.4.2.0 WITHOUT --force completed EXIT 0 (90x); 'Purged 383 leaked dev artifact(s)' removed seeded .claude-session-ring.jsonl + stale.py.backup while venv survived, leaked path 404 over HTTPS (emq/qlr); smoke probe reported '1 warning(s), 0 failures' with the credential-less downloader downgraded to a warning (bqe). 32 new regression tests; full suite 5356 passed.

title: Stale old-account DKIM TXT still published at resend._domainkey.thebosco.club
description:
Found 2026-08-03 after rotating the Resend API key to a new Resend account.

STATE: TWO TXT records exist at resend._domainkey.thebosco.club:
  - p=...CodY+SIWqwwzlXxv/MZIERu9y5DyzoRiDPARhxX7pNGCzyhit...  (NEW account, correct, keep)
  - p=...DdXDCfM1P7EHipC7MaIWVsNnwkTSYKDUs/Jucr4t5ALf8IH8x...  (OLD account, delete)

The new record was ADDED alongside the old rather than replacing it.

WHY IT MATTERS:
1. SECURITY (primary): the old Resend API key is still unrevoked — confirmed sending HTTP 200 as library@thebosco.club on 2026-08-03. With the old DKIM record still published, the OLD account retains the ability to send fully DKIM-signed mail as thebosco.club. Deleting this record severs that capability regardless of whether the key revocation is ever completed.
2. CORRECTNESS: RFC 6376 s3.6.2.2 leaves multi-key-record behavior unspecified — a verifier MAY pick one record or cycle. Gmail cycles (test message delivered to INBOX, not spam). A verifier that picks the first record and stops gets the old key and fails DKIM. Receiver-dependent, intermittent.
3. LATENT: _dmarc.thebosco.club is currently p=none, so DKIM failure does not bounce mail today. Tightening DMARC to quarantine/reject before fixing this would turn it into live delivery failure.

FIX: delete the TXT record at resend._domainkey.thebosco.club containing 'DdXDCfM1P7EHipC7MaIWVs'. Keep the CodY+SIWqww one.

BLOCKED BY: Audiobook-Manager-e7x — the Cloudflare Global API Key is stale (403/9103), so this cannot be automated until a working scoped token exists. Manual edit via Cloudflare dashboard is the interim path.

ALSO NOTED (minor): send.thebosco.club still carries 'v=spf1 include:amazonses.com ~all' with no matching DKIM — vestigial from the old subdomain setup, harmless, remove opportunistically.
close_reason:
Resolved 2026-08-03. Deleted old-account DKIM TXT (id 60dfb1ddfd25f70d64a125684cc8289a, created 2026-03-04, TTL 120, fragment DdXDCfM1) from zone 24558cb1f70c1a803c249d79a56bde7c using CLOUDFLARE_DNS_ZONE_API_TOKEN.

VERIFIED:
- Cloudflare API: exactly 1 TXT remains — id 07bd6e0eeedbc905c939f02a45996f9e, fragment CodY+SIW (new account, created 2026-08-03).
- All 4 authoritative NS IPs over TCP: 1 record each, CodY+SIW; old DdXDCf fragment absent.
- Email unbroken: end-to-end send via LIVE audiobook-api worker env + installed resolve_secret() delivered to INBOX (abm-postdkim-115011), user-confirmed.
- Record JSON backed up before deletion (DKIM public keys are public data).

METHOD NOTE: initial UDP verification was WRONG and nearly produced a false conclusion. This host's network transparently intercepts UDP:53 — dig to 192.0.2.1 (TEST-NET-1) returns answers, responses lack the aa flag, +norecurse yields ANSWER:0. UDP 'authoritative' queries were served from the router cache at 192.168.86.1 and showed the already-deleted record. Use dig +tcp plus the provider API on this host.

DEPENDENCY CORRECTION: this issue had been marked as blocked by Audiobook-Manager-e7x on the assumption the dead Cloudflare credential prevented automating the DNS edit. That was wrong — dedicated zone-scoped tokens were created, so the work proceeded independently. Dependency removed.

title: Cloudflare Global API Key in /etc/audiobooks/cloudflare-api-token is stale — purge-cache endpoint is a zombie
description:
Discovered 2026-08-03 while diagnosing a Resend key rotation.

EVIDENCE: The credential parses correctly (37 hex chars, CF_AUTH_EMAIL=gjbr@pm.me) but Cloudflare rejects it:
  GET /client/v4/zones?name=thebosco.club -> HTTP 403, code 9103 'Unknown X-Auth-Key or X-Auth-Email'

WHAT IT CLAIMS TO DO: back POST /api/system/purge-cache in audiobook-api (per the header comment in the credential file).
EVIDENCE IT DOES NOT: any purge call authenticating with this key gets 403. The endpoint cannot have worked since the key was rotated/revoked upstream; no journal evidence of successful purge.

TWO DEFECTS, NOT ONE:
1. Credential is dead -> feature silently broken (fails closed, no alerting).
2. It is a GLOBAL API KEY (full account access) where a scoped token (Zone > Cache Purge only) is required by ~/.claude/rules/security.md least-privilege. Even once refreshed, it must be replaced with a scoped token, not a new global key.

BLAST RADIUS: Audiobook-Manager-017 (admin Refresh button) depends on a working purge path and would ship broken.

FIX: issue a scoped Cloudflare token with Zone>Cache Purge for thebosco.club, store per security.md, update the file format (currently CF_GLOBAL_API_KEY/CF_AUTH_EMAIL -> Bearer token), and verify with an actual purge call returning success.
notes:
=== 2026-08-26 DIAGNOSIS — ISSUE IS DEEPER THAN FILED ===

FINDING 1: the SCOPED replacement token is ALSO invalid, not just the legacy Global key.
  A read-only call to the Cloudflare token-verify endpoint, using the token from
  the runtime-derived purge-token file, returns:
      success=False, errors=[{code: 1000, message: Invalid API Token}]
  So BOTH Cloudflare credentials on this host are dead:
    - legacy Global API Key  -> HTTP 403, code 9103 (original evidence, Aug 3)
    - scoped purge token     -> code 1000 Invalid API Token (new, Aug 26)
  purge-cache remains a zombie. The derive-service-secret PLUMBING works (file
  present, mode 0400 audiobooks:audiobooks, populated at service start) but the
  VALUE it derives from the canonical credential store is itself stale. Deriving
  a dead secret correctly still yields a dead secret — the mechanism was
  verified, the outcome never was. Classic success-is-never-self-reported.

FINDING 2: single-canonical-source violation in the pointer wiring.
  The purge-token pointer in audiobooks.conf (line 119) names a path under the
  system config tree, but derive-service-secret writes its file under the
  runtime tree. Two separate files, same basename, different directories; the
  app reads the hand-made config-tree copy (dated Aug 3), NOT the derived
  runtime copy that the service actually regenerates at every start. This is
  exactly the drift the infrastructure rule exists to prevent. The pointer must
  aim at the runtime path, and the config-tree copy must be deleted rather than
  left as a shadow.

STILL OUTSTANDING from the original filing (re-verified today):
  - audiobooks.conf line 51 still has an INLINE SMTP password. resolve_secret()
    gives inline precedence over the pointer variant, so the pointer form would
    be ignored even if added. The inline line must be deleted, not supplemented.
  - The legacy Global-key pointer (line 73) still names the stale key file.
  - The system config dir still holds the Global-key file (189B, Mar 26, mode
    0640), a purge-token copy, THREE zero-byte leftovers (deepl / runpod / smtp),
    and FIVE stale audiobooks.conf backups dated Feb-Aug which may carry
    pre-rotation credentials and should be treated as credential-bearing residue.

BLOCKED ON OPERATOR: a valid Cloudflare API token scoped to Zone > Cache Purge
must be minted and written to the canonical credential store before the cutover
can be completed and proven end-to-end. Everything else is mechanical and ready.
close_reason:
ROOT CAUSE: not an expired key. The derive-secrets drop-in named the credential-store entry CLOUDFLARE_PURGE_TOKEN, which is a stale orphan; the operator's live scoped Zone>Cache-Purge token is stored as CF_TOKEN_CACHE_PURGE. derive-service-secret faithfully wrote a dead value to the runtime path at every start, resolution fell through to the legacy Global API Key, and that key had been revoked upstream. Both credentials dead => zombie endpoint.

PROOF (live Cloudflare API, token-verify endpoint):
  CLOUDFLARE_PURGE_TOKEN -> success=False, code 1000 Invalid API Token
  CF_TOKEN_CACHE_PURGE   -> success=True, status=active
Before restart the derived runtime token verified False; after installing the
corrected drop-in and restarting, it verified True/active, mode 0400
audiobooks:audiobooks. _resolve_cf_auth_headers() returns 'Bearer (scoped
token)' rather than the X-Auth-Key fallback, and a real purge_everything call
against the configured zone returned success=True.

FALSIFICATION: removed the legacy Global-key file, restarted, re-ran. The
legacy lookup now returns (None, None) and purge STILL returns success=True --
the scoped path stands alone and was not being masked by the fallback.

ALSO FIXED (single-canonical-source): the purge pointer in audiobooks.conf
named a path in the system config tree while derive-service-secret writes to
the runtime tree -- two files, same basename, and the app was reading the
hand-made Aug 3 copy rather than the one regenerated at every start. Pointer
repointed at the runtime path; the config-tree copy and the stale Global-key
file were both removed at the operator's instruction (all credentials belong
only in the canonical store). The legacy CF_TOKEN_FILE pointer was removed
from the config with an explanatory comment.

Fix committed as db856dbf including a CHANGELOG entry. Unblocks
Audiobook-Manager-017.

NOT DONE: the SMTP side of the original filing (inline SMTP_PASS still present,
SMTP_PASS_FILE absent). Deliberately deferred to Audiobook-Manager-9nu, which
migrates this project to the credential-less local mail relay and deletes the
concept of an SMTP password entirely -- doing the pointer cutover now would
build something 9nu demolishes. RESEND_KEY_LIBRARY was verified to be a real
store entry, so the smtp-pass derive does not have the same wrong-name bug.

title: Resend API key lives in /etc/audiobooks/audiobooks.conf (x4 copies) instead of ~/.config/api-keys.env
description:
SECURITY / rules violation found 2026-08-03. The global rule (~/.claude/rules/security.md) is that ALL API keys live in ~/.config/api-keys.env with services sourcing from there. The Resend send key does not.

CURRENT STATE:
- /etc/audiobooks/audiobooks.conf holds SMTP_PASS=<resend key> inline (SMTP_HOST=smtp.resend.com, SMTP_PORT=587, SMTP_USER=resend, SMTP_FROM=library@thebosco.club).
- THREE further copies sit beside it in the same directory: audiobooks.conf.bak002, audiobooks.conf.bak-20260413-021329, audiobooks.conf.pre-vastai-backlog-20260423-231111.bak. Each is a separate disclosure surface and none is rotated when the key rotates.
- ~/.config/api-keys.env contains NO Resend entry at all (verified by hash: the extracted value is the empty string). So this is not drift between two live copies -- the canonical store is simply empty and the only copies are the non-canonical ones.

ALSO: the key was printed in cleartext into a Claude session transcript on 2026-08-03 (~/.claude/projects/-hddRaid1-ClaudeCodeProjects-cachyos-sentinel/<session>.jsonl) by an over-broad grep of the config file. Operator advised to rotate at https://resend.com/api-keys -- rotation is what closes it; the transcript copy becomes inert once the old key is deleted.

WORK:
1. Rotate the Resend key (delete the old one, do not just add a new one).
2. Add it to ~/.config/api-keys.env with the service/purpose/scope comment the rule requires.
3. Change the consumer to source it from there rather than carry its own copy -- same pattern as parse_pbridge_smtp() in DAS-Backup-Manager/scripts/backup-run.sh, which is the reference implementation for reading a canonical credential file at runtime.
4. Remove SMTP_PASS from audiobooks.conf and shred the three .bak copies (they are stale config backups, and the tree is in git + BTRFS snapshots).
5. Audit for further copies -- a repo-tree scan was started and timed out, so the Audiobook-Manager working tree is UNVERIFIED, not confirmed clean.

Note for whoever picks this up: keeping backups of a credentials file in the same directory as the live file is the pattern ~/.claude/rules/development-tools.md warns about. Put backups outside the directory, or rely on git/snapshots.
notes: 2026-08-05: canonical store already held the key as RESEND_KEY_LIBRARY (sha256 prefix 8e9ea55997ec matches conf SMTP_PASS) — no duplicate entry added, ACL (u:root:rw) preserved. Working-tree scan for the credential value: zero matches (rg --no-ignore --hidden -F, paths-only, value never echoed). Remaining work = the prod cutover checklist recorded on Audiobook-Manager-ac2 (items 2-5): SMTP_PASS inline removal happens there. Closes together with ac2 after the post-promote email proof.
close_reason:
Closed 2026-08-26 on operator instruction; Resend keys rotated for this project, cachyos-sentinel and DAS-Backup.

ROTATION PROVEN, not taken on trust — and proven by an outage it caused. After the rotation, ~/.config/api-keys.env was newer (14:37:47) than /etc/postfix/sasl_passwd.lmdb (2026-08-18), so the relay was still presenting the revoked keys. A probe message produced:
  535 Authentication credentials invalid  ->  status=deferred
which is direct evidence the old Resend credentials are dead. Re-ran the sync tool (3 sender entries, postmap, postfix reload) and flushed; the SAME message id 42AC614FF235 went
  status=sent (250 fa581154-cb33-4da4-99aa-30ecda4e490e)
with the queue draining empty. Outage window was ~2 minutes and latent — nothing had attempted to send between the rotation and the check.

ITEMS 1-3 AND 5: done. The key was already canonical as RESEND_KEY_LIBRARY; the working-tree scan came back clean on 2026-08-05; and item 3 was OVERTAKEN by Audiobook-Manager-9nu, which removed the consumer's need to hold an SMTP credential at all rather than merely teaching it to source one — a better outcome than this issue asked for.

ITEM 4: SMTP_PASS was removed from the live /etc/audiobooks/audiobooks.conf today. The .bak copies were NOT removed and are carried forward under a new issue rather than dropped — their Resend and RunPod values are now inert, but they still contain a LIVE DeepL Pro key (verified HTTP 200 against api.deepl.com), which is outside this issue's stated scope.

title: ShellPlayer: chapter-skip buttons must work for ALL playback paths, not just streaming-translation
description:
library/web-v2/js/shell.js::ShellPlayer hides #sp-skip-back-chapter / #sp-skip-forward-chapter for the English single-stream path because chapter info wasn't surfaced. With the new GET /api/audiobooks/<id>/chapters endpoint (sister bd issue), the player can fetch chapter boundaries on book load and use them.

**Fix scope**:
1. ShellPlayer::playBook — fetch /api/audiobooks/<id>/chapters, store as this.chapters array (silently no-op on 404)
2. Drop the 'streamingTranslate.isStreaming() OR translatedEntries' visibility guard. NEW logic: show skip buttons whenever this.chapters.length > 0
3. _skipBackChapter — find chapter where start_ms <= currentTime*1000 < end_ms; if (currentTime*1000 - start_ms) > RESTART_THRESHOLD_SEC*1000 → audio.currentTime = start_ms/1000 (restart current chapter); else → audio.currentTime = previous chapter's start_ms/1000 (skip to previous chapter)
4. _skipForwardChapter — audio.currentTime = next chapter's start_ms/1000
5. Hide buttons when chapters API returned empty (genuine 'no chapter info' — keep current 'don't expose non-functional controls' principle)

**Files**:
- library/web-v2/js/shell.js — ShellPlayer.playBook fetch+store, _skipBackChapter / _skipForwardChapter rewrites, visibility logic
- library/tests/test_chapter_nav_wiring.py — extend existing tests: 'buttons visible when chapters.length > 0 regardless of streaming path', 'skip-back from mid-chapter restarts current chapter', 'skip-back near chapter start jumps to previous', 'skip-forward jumps to next chapter start', 'buttons hidden when chapters API returns empty/404'

**Existing v8.3.10.1 streaming-translation path behavior**: PRESERVE. Don't break the streaming MSE jumpToChapter / translatedEntries handling — the new chapter array becomes a third trigger for visibility, doesn't replace the existing two.

**i18n**: the existing data-i18n-title attributes on the buttons are unchanged — works as-is.

Bundle into v8.3.10.2 tweak release (Bosco direction). Depends on the chapters endpoint issue (sister).

title: add /api/audiobooks/<id>/chapters endpoint exposing per-book chapter boundaries
description:
The English single-stream audio path (/stream/<id>) has no client-side chapter info, so the v8.3.10.1 chapter-skip buttons (Audiobook-Manager-9by) are deliberately hidden — making them useless for ~90% of the library which is English audiobooks. **Fix scope**: New endpoint GET /api/audiobooks/<id>/chapters returning JSON {chapters: [{index, start_ms, end_ms, title?}, ...]}. Lazy ffprobe + in-memory cache (small, immutable per file). 404 when file has no chapters (rare — mostly podcasts).

- library/backend/api_modular/audiobooks.py (or new chapters.py blueprint sibling) — new route

title: audiobook-translation-monitor-live hits StartLimit hourly: Burst=5 blocks 30s timer
description:
Discovered on prod 2026-05-02 while verifying the v8.3.10 GPU pod monitoring services (the new translation-monitor-live and translation-monitor-sampler services that watch for stuck/dead/failed claims).

**Symptom:** `audiobook-translation-monitor-live.service` cycles between 'failed (start-limit-hit)' for 4-5 minute stretches and brief recovery to a single successful run, repeating every ~5 minutes. journalctl shows continuous 'Start request repeated too quickly' / 'Failed with result start-limit-hit' lines from systemd.

**Math:**
- Timer: `OnUnitActiveSec=30s` → 2 firings/minute = 10 firings per 5min window
- Service: `StartLimitBurst=5`, `StartLimitIntervalSec=300` → max 5 starts per 5min = 1 start/minute
- Result: timer fills the burst quota in 150s, next 150s of firings are blocked. Live tier runs ~5×/5min instead of intended 10×/5min — 50% miss rate on 'claim reset, retry sweep'.

**Why it matters:** these are the exact services Bosco asked about — the 'monitor for stuck/dead/failed GPU pods' wiring from v8.3.10. They reset stuck `streaming_segments.state='processing'` rows, retry failed segments, and clean up orphaned worker claims. Half of those sweep cycles are silently being dropped.

**Fix (rolled into staged v8.3.10.1):** raise `StartLimitBurst` from 5 to 20 in `systemd/audiobook-translation-monitor-live.service`. 20 starts per 300s = 1 every 15s, 4× headroom over the 30s timer cadence. Still enforces a runaway cap if the service entered a true fail-loop (saturates at 20 in 5min instead of the healthy 10/5min). `StartLimitIntervalSec=300` unchanged.

Sampler tier (`OnUnitActiveSec=5min`, `StartLimitBurst=5`, `Interval=600`) is healthy — only 2 starts per 600s window, well under the 5-burst limit. No change needed.

**Source:** Bosco's question 2026-05-02 'are the new services to watch for stuck, dead, or failed GPU pods working as expected in prod?' — turned out the answer was 'sampler yes, live no.'
close_reason: Fixed in v8.3.10.1: StartLimitBurst raised from 5 to 20 on audiobook-translation-monitor-live.service. Math: 30s timer × 5min window = 10 firings, but Burst=5 only allowed 5 — half the sweeps silently dropped. Bumped Burst gives 4× cadence headroom. 6 regression tests in test_translation_monitor_systemd.py guard the math going forward.

title: user_listening_history rows balloon — every 5s position save creates new row
description:
Diagnosed 2026-05-02 from Bosco's prod screenshot: `A Dirty Job` shows 3,671 listens, `The Long Fall` shows 1,102. Root cause is in `library/backend/api_modular/position_sync.py::_update_listening_history`: every position save (every 5s during active playback) sets `session.ended_at = now`, which makes the next call's `get_open_session` find no open session (because ended_at is no longer NULL) and INSERT a fresh row. Effect: ~12 rows/min × hours of playback = thousands of rows per book.

Math: 3671 rows × 5s/row = ~5h continuous playback recorded as 3671 "listens".

**Code fix** (rolled into staged v8.3.10.1): widen `get_open_session` predicate from `ended_at IS NULL` to `ended_at IS NULL OR ended_at > now - 30 minutes`. New `SESSION_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MINUTES` constant. Continuous playback within 30-min windows reuses the same row; 30+ min idle creates a new session.

**Data repair** (also rolled in): one-shot data-migrations script that collapses contiguous history rows (gap < 30 min) into single sessions per (user_id, audiobook_id, session window). Preserves earliest started_at and latest ended_at; sums duration_listened_ms.

Affects: TOP LISTENED stats card on `utilities.html`, total_listens count, active_users count (less affected — DISTINCT user_id collapses).
close_reason: Code fix in v8.3.10.1: get_open_session predicate widened to 30-min idle window with localtime-aware SQL. Stops row explosion. Existing prod data repair tracked as separate follow-up (auth.db SQLCipher-encrypted, needs different tooling than the standard data-migrations framework).

title: Sampler pipeline silently dead since 2026-06-06 — 14 sampler_jobs stuck 'pending' for ~4 months with no error recorded
description:

- systemctl is-active audiobook-translation-monitor-sampler.timer -> active

WHY IT MATTERS: this is the silent-failure shape in ~/.claude/rules/verification.md

subsystem is installed, scheduled, reporting healthy, and doing nothing.

INVESTIGATE:
1. Why does the retry path never write to sampler_jobs.error? A swallowed exception

2. What changed on/around 2026-06-06? Correlate with releases and dependency bumps.

Therefore either (a) diagnose od0 while a backend is available, or (b) accept that it stays open and unverifiable until audio translation is next enabled.

DO NOT close this issue merely because disabling the timer stopped it being visible. That is masking, not fixing. See docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-26-audio-translation-capability-flag.md (PARKED) for the wider context.

title: Dockerfile jq/openssl pins stale against Trixie security updates
description: Docker Build Check failed with 'jq : Depends: libjq1 (= 1.7.1-6+deb13u2) but 1.7.1-6+deb13u3 is to be installed'. Distinct from the earlier ffmpeg/curl pin drifts, which failed as 'Version not found' after the pinned version was purged. Here the pin still exists: apt-get upgrade -y advances the UNPINNED libjq1 to deb13u3 while the pinned jq=deb13u2 requires libjq1 at exactly deb13u2. Any pinned package whose unpinned shared library takes a security update fails this way. openssl was also stale (3.5.6-1~deb13u2 -> 3.5.7-1~deb13u2). This had been broken independently of the mando issue and was invisible because Docker Build Check was not a required status check and main was not re-running CI.
design: Advance the pin rather than additionally pinning the shared library. Re-capture all pins with the command documented in the Dockerfile header, against the digest in FROM. CVE notes at the top of the Dockerfile cover ffmpeg/mesa/mbedtls/ncurses/systemd and are unaffected; both bumps move onto security updates.
acceptance_criteria: apt layer builds clean against the pinned digest, reporting OpenSSL 3.5.7 and jq-1.7; Docker Build Check green on main.
close_reason: Fixed and verified on main 3170685d: CI, Python Security & Quality and Security Checks all green. 12 required status checks live on main (strict), required-context list cross-checked against actual check-run names (zero mismatches). Daily schedule + workflow_dispatch added to ci.yml and security-checks.yml. mando restored to >=0.7.1,<0.8 with a dependabot.yml ignore for >=0.8. jq -> 1.7.1-6+deb13u3, openssl -> 3.5.7-1~deb13u2, apt layer build-verified against the FROM digest.

title: _NEVER_SHIP_EXCLUDES has no pattern for *.backup/*.bak/*.orig/*~ dev-editor artifacts
description:
Discovered during Phase 10a staged-release VM testing of v8.4.2.0 on
test-audiobook-cachyos, alongside Audiobook-Manager-emq (the .claude*
rsync-delete-protection issue).

The project's own working tree had an untracked, gitignored stray file
library/backend/api_modular/auth.py.backup (199KB, mtime 2026-03-29 --
an old dev-session leftover, gitignored via library/.gitignore's `*.backup`
pattern so git never saw it). _NEVER_SHIP_EXCLUDES in upgrade.sh has no
`--exclude='*.backup'` (or *.bak / *.orig / *~) entry, so it is NOT a
gitignore-aware sync -- rsync copies everything present in the working tree
except what's explicitly listed in _NEVER_SHIP_EXCLUDES, regardless of
.gitignore.

Confirmed via `stat` on the VM: the file's Birth time matched today's
deploy exactly (rsync freshly copied it), Modify time preserved from the
source (2026-03-29) -- i.e. this is not a stale artifact, it was actively
shipped by THIS deploy to
/opt/audiobooks/library/backend/api_modular/auth.py.backup.

Impact is lower than Audiobook-Manager-emq (backend/api_modular/ is Python
source imported by the Flask app, not served as static files, so this
specific file is not directly HTTP-fetchable the way web-v2/ artifacts are)
but still real:
 - Ships a stale, potentially security-relevant historical copy of the auth
   module (199KB) to every single install, forever, as long as any
   developer's working tree has a *.backup/*.bak/*.orig/*~ file anywhere
   under the synced trees (lib/, library/, converter/).
 - If any future feature adds a source-browsing, log-bundling, or
   support-tarball endpoint under backend/, this file becomes exposed with
   zero additional code changes.
 - Pure dead weight / attack-surface bloat with no functional purpose.

Suggested fix: add editor/dev-backup glob patterns to _NEVER_SHIP_EXCLUDES:
  --exclude='*.backup'
  --exclude='*.bak'
  --exclude='*.orig'
  --exclude='*~'
Same "purge already-shipped copies too" caveat as Audiobook-Manager-emq
applies -- adding the exclude alone won't clean up copies already on a
target's disk from a prior deploy.

Cleaned up locally (untracked, gitignored, deleted -- not a release blocker
by itself, but the missing exclude pattern is).
close_reason: Fixed in staged v8.4.2.0 (commit 6702c4de) and PROVEN end-to-end on test-audiobook-cachyos: a real --remote deploy 8.4.0.1->8.4.2.0 WITHOUT --force completed EXIT 0 (90x); 'Purged 383 leaked dev artifact(s)' removed seeded .claude-session-ring.jsonl + stale.py.backup while venv survived, leaked path 404 over HTTPS (emq/qlr); smoke probe reported '1 warning(s), 0 failures' with the credential-less downloader downgraded to a warning (bqe). 32 new regression tests; full suite 5356 passed.

title: smoke_probe.sh fails every VM deploy: audiobook-downloader.service always 'failed' (no Audible creds) on credential-less test VMs
description:
Discovered during Phase 10a staged-release VM testing of v8.4.2.0 on
test-audiobook-cachyos (192.168.122.104).

./upgrade.sh --from-project . --remote 192.168.122.104 --yes --force
successfully rsyncs the release, restarts services, applies migration
014_original_publish_year, and updates VERSION to 8.4.2.0 (confirmed via
`curl http://192.168.122.104:5001/api/system/version` -> {"version":"8.4.2.0"}
and `cat /opt/audiobooks/VERSION` -> 8.4.2.0). But upgrade.sh's own
scripts/smoke_probe.sh gate then fails the whole run:

  ✗ audiobook-downloader.service: failed
  === Smoke probe: 1 FAILURE(S), 0 warning(s) ===
  === Post-upgrade smoke probe FAILED — upgrade aborted ===
  Remote upgrade failed (exit code 1)

Root cause: audiobook-downloader.service exits 1 with
"error: Config file /var/lib/audiobooks/.audible/config.toml does not exists"
-- this VM (per testing.md's CRITICAL: Test/QA Data Isolation rule) MUST NOT
have real Audible credentials, so audiobook-downloader.timer firing (it runs
every few minutes) will ALWAYS leave the service in `failed` (not `inactive`)
state on this VM, forever, on every future deploy. smoke_probe.sh's
_probe_systemd() treats "failed" as a hard failure for every unit -- there's
an _expected_inactive allowlist (downloader is in it) but that only covers
the `inactive` case-branch; the `failed)` branch always calls _fail
regardless of unit name.

Confirmed pre-existing, not a v8.4.2.0 regression: audiobook-downloader.service
was already `loaded failed failed` before this deploy started (Phase 2
baseline check, same missing-config.toml error).

Impact: every future /test Phase 10a run against this VM (or any credential-

title: Migrate all email from direct-Resend SMTP and Bridge to the local mail relay (library@thebosco.club)
description:
Move every mail path in this project onto the host's local relay at 127.0.0.1:25, sending as library@thebosco.club. Consumers stop handling credentials, TLS, and retries entirely.

READ FIRST — authoritative, do not redesign:
  /hddRaid1/ClaudeCodeProjects/cachyos-sentinel/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-02-email-transport-design.md

DEPENDENCY — DO NOT START BEFORE THIS
The relay does not exist yet. Verified 2026-08-05: postfix inactive, nothing listening on 127.0.0.1:25, no /etc/postfix/sasl_passwd. Blocked on the cachyos-sentinel relay-deployment issue. Until it lands, this project keeps working exactly as today — nothing breaks by waiting.
Check before starting:  ss -ltn | grep ':25 '

WHY
Two different transports are in use here, and both are wrong for automation:
  - scripts/email-report.py talks to smtp.resend.com:587 DIRECTLY, doing its own
    STARTTLS, its own login, and holding a credential.
  - The Bridge path is session-bound: KWallet only unlocks at a real login, so after
    an unattended reboot mail is silently lost.
The relay fixes both. It is a root service with credentials under /etc, needs no
session, and queues for days if the uplink is down rather than dropping mail.

CREDENTIAL — ALREADY EXISTS, DO NOT CREATE ANOTHER, DO NOT READ IT
RESEND_KEY_LIBRARY is already in ~/.config/api-keys.env.

This project MUST NOT read it. It never touches a mail credential again. The key is consumed only by /etc/postfix/sasl_passwd, generated by /usr/local/sbin/mail-relay-sync-credentials, which already lists library@thebosco.club. Submission to the relay is unauthenticated plaintext on loopback; Postfix authenticates upstream by envelope sender.

thebosco.club is domain-verified at Resend, so library@thebosco.club is already a valid sender. No address creation needed.

CHANGES

1. scripts/email-report.py  (lines 119-134)
   Currently: host defaults smtp.resend.com, port 587, user "resend",
   password from conf or resolve_secret("SMTP_PASS"), then starttls() + login().
   Change to: host 127.0.0.1, port 25, NO starttls(), NO login(), no password lookup.
   Set from_addr to library@thebosco.club (replacing audiobooks@localhost).
   Delete the SMTP_USER / SMTP_PASS handling in this file outright — do not leave it
   as an unused fallback. A dead credential path is how stale copies survive.

2. library/backend/api_modular/auth_email.py  (lines 40-44)
   Already defaults to localhost:25, which is nearly right. Remove the
   resolve_secret("SMTP_PASS") call and any login()/starttls() on this path, and
   change SMTP_FROM's default from noreply@localhost to library@thebosco.club.

3. Config and installers
   Remove SMTP_HOST / SMTP_PORT / SMTP_USER / SMTP_PASS / SMTP_PASS_FILE plumbing
   from install.sh, upgrade.sh, scripts/install-manifest.sh, scripts/setup-email.sh,
   and /etc/audiobooks/audiobooks.conf. Grep for SMTP_ across the repo and remove
   every consumer; the relay needs none of it. If setup-email.sh exists only to
   configure these, delete the script.

4. Delete the on-disk credential files this project no longer needs, and remove any
   *_FILE pointers to them from audiobooks.conf.

VERIFY — PROVE IT, DO NOT ASSERT IT
  - Trigger a real report email and confirm INBOX delivery, sender library@thebosco.club.
  - Trigger a real auth email (the login/OTP path) and confirm delivery.
  - Prove the unattended property, which is the whole point: stop Bridge
    (systemctl --user stop protonmail-bridge), confirm 127.0.0.1:1025 is gone, then
    send both kinds of mail again and confirm they still arrive.
  - grep the repo for SMTP_PASS, smtp.resend.com, starttls, and pbridge — all should
    be gone from code and config. Any survivor is a path that will rot.

NOTE ON e7x
Audiobook-Manager-e7x tracks the stale Global API Key in /etc/audiobooks/cloudflare-api-token. Unrelated credential, same disease: a hand-copied secret with no rotation mechanism. Deleting mail credentials here does not close e7x.

this project has ZERO references to pbridge and ZERO to port 1025. Proton Bridge

SCOPE PROVED MUCH SMALLER THAN FILED:
  - The relay was already provisioned for this sender (sasl_passwd carries a

  - 4 of the 5 senders already wrapped BOTH starttls() and login() in

  - Only scripts/email-report.py had unconditional starttls()+login(). It also

  - Committed afb81180 with CHANGELOG entry, pushed.

PROOF (delivery, not queueing): a real message sent as the audiobooks user via
the patched script logged
  from=<library@thebosco.club> relay=smtp.resend.com[54.157.71.137]:587
  tls=secure dsn=2.0.0 status=sent (250 3c1e29c1-1c67-450e-b871-80f8f4ed9bdf)
and the mail queue drained empty. smtplib printing 'Email sent' only proves

Separately, auth_email.py::_get_email_config() under the live service

title: Migrate audiobook-api to derive-service-secret for unprivileged access to the canonical credential store
description:
Adopt cloudflare-manager's derive-service-secret so audiobook-api stops depending on hand-copied credential files under /etc/audiobooks/.

WHY THIS EXISTS: audiobook-api runs as User=audiobooks (uid 935, nologin). /home/bosco is mode 710, which blocks directory traversal before any file mode is consulted, so that account cannot read the canonical store ~/.config/api-keys.env at all — verified 2026-08-03. With no sanctioned mechanism, credentials were hand-copied into /etc/audiobooks/, and hand-copies have no way to track rotation. That is exactly how /etc/audiobooks/cloudflare-api-token came to hold a pre-rotation Global API Key (Audiobook-Manager-e7x).

/etc/audiobooks/cloudflare-purge-token is the SAME PATTERN and will drift the same way at the next rotation. It is correct today only because it was made today.

THE TOOL SHIPPED 2026-08-05, installed at /usr/bin/derive-service-secret (root:root 0755). It runs as root from ExecStartPre=+, derives exactly one variable from the canonical store, and writes it to /run/<svc>/ as 0400 svc:svc. Regeneration at every service start is what makes drift structurally impossible. It refuses any target that does not RESOLVE under /run (canonicalized, so .. traversal and symlinked components cannot land a secret on snapshotted storage), and fails closed on a variable that is missing or empty — including empty only after quote-stripping. 30-case suite, gated on every commit in cloudflare-manager.

WORK:
1. audiobook-api.service gains:
     RuntimeDirectory=audiobooks
     ExecStartPre=+/usr/bin/derive-service-secret CLOUDFLARE_PURGE_TOKEN \\
         /run/audiobooks/cloudflare-purge-token audiobooks
2. Repoint CLOUDFLARE_PURGE_TOKEN_FILE at the /run path in audiobooks.conf.
3. Verify a real purge succeeds against the deployed install.
4. Then delete BOTH /etc/audiobooks/cloudflare-api-token AND
   /etc/audiobooks/cloudflare-purge-token, and drop CF_TOKEN_FILE.

KNOWN OBSTACLE — needs a decision before any Bridge/SMTP credential moves the same way: ~/.claude/rules/infrastructure.md says ALL projects MUST read pbridge.conf at runtime, no exceptions, and names this project. But audiobooks cannot read pbridge.conf for the same 710 reason, and derive-service-secret parses VAR=value lines, not pbridge.conf's colon-indented two-block format. Nothing breaks today (the only current consumer, DAS backup-run.sh, runs as root). Note /etc/audiobooks/smtp-pass already exists as a 0-byte audiobooks-owned file, so the collision is closer than it looks.

RULE: ~/.claude/rules/infrastructure.md, 'Unprivileged service users and the canonical credential store'.
FILED because Audiobook-Manager-e7x carries the detail in a NOTE, and bd search indexes title and description only — searching 'derive-service-secret' or 'unprivileged' returned nothing, so the mandated existence check would have reported this untracked.
notes:
REPO-SIDE COMPLETE 2026-08-05 (staged for 8.4.2.0): audiobook-api.service gains RuntimeDirectory=audiobooks (0750); NEW template systemd/audiobook-api-derive-secrets.conf.example (ExecStartPre lines for CLOUDFLARE_PURGE_TOKEN and RESEND_KEY_LIBRARY — note the store's real entry name, NOT RESEND_API_KEY); install.sh+upgrade.sh conditionally install the drop-in when /usr/bin/derive-service-secret exists; docs updated (EMAIL-SETUP.md hardened-setup section, ARCHITECTURE.md credential resolution).

POST-PROMOTE PROD CUTOVER CHECKLIST (blocks closing this + aiq):
1. Deploy via upgrade.sh (installs unit + drop-in + manifest-derived stubs; daemon-reload)
2. /etc/audiobooks/audiobooks.conf: SMTP_PASS_FILE=/run/audiobooks/smtp-pass, CLOUDFLARE_PURGE_TOKEN_FILE=/run/audiobooks/cloudflare-purge-token; REMOVE inline SMTP_PASS= line (inline wins over pointer); drop CF_TOKEN_FILE
3. Restart audiobook-api; verify /run/audiobooks/{smtp-pass,cloudflare-purge-token} exist 0400 audiobooks:audiobooks; smtp-pass content sha256 prefix must be 8e9ea55997ec
4. E2E via user pathway: test email send + real CDN purge from web UI

title: CI re-downloads 95.5 MB of apt packages on every matrix leg with no caching — one slow mirror stalls a run for 46 minutes
description: ci.yml 'Install system dependencies' runs 'sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y libsqlcipher-dev ffmpeg' uncached on all three Python matrix legs. ffmpeg's dependency tree is 95.5 MB, so a full CI run pulls ~286 MB from azure.archive.ubuntu.com every time. On 2026-08-03 the mirror degraded to 34.4 kB/s and the 3.13 leg spent 46m16s in that single step ('Fetched 95.5 MB in 46min 16s'), turning a ~4 minute job into 50m32s. The job ultimately SUCCEEDED (5112 passed, 130 skipped) — nothing was broken, but the run was indistinguishable from a hang for 45 minutes and would have been cancelled had it been watched less carefully. Options: cache /var/cache/apt/archives via actions/cache keyed on the package list; install only the leg that needs ffmpeg; or move to a prebuilt container image with the system deps baked in.
notes:
INVESTIGATION 2026-08-05 — ffmpeg necessity settled empirically.

RUNTIME: ffmpeg is unambiguously required by the product. Dockerfile pins ffmpeg=7:7.1.5-0+deb13u1; install.sh hard-exits if ffmpeg/ffprobe are absent and warns if libopus is missing. 9 production call sites across scanner/metadata_utils.py, localization/{chapters,queue}.py, backend/api_modular/{audiobooks,translated_audio,streaming_translate,utilities_conversion}.py. NOT a candidate for removal anywhere.

CI TEST SUITE: ran the full suite in python:3.13-slim-trixie with libsqlcipher-dev but deliberately NO ffmpeg. Result: 13 failed, 5089 passed, 140 skipped (1206s). Causal attribution of the 13:
  - 3 genuinely require the ffmpeg binary (traceback: FileNotFoundError ... 'ffmpeg'):
      test_streaming_tts_consolidation.py::test_synthesize_silent_segment_audio_creates_valid_webm
      test_streaming_tts_consolidation.py::test_process_segment_no_speech_falls_back_to_silent_segment
      test_streaming_tts_consolidation.py::test_process_segment_runs_full_stt_when_vtt_content_empty
  - 6 need 'node', not ffmpeg (test_streaming_threshold_cap.py) — container artifact, GH runners ship Node
  - 3 fail because the container runs as root, so permission-error tests cannot trigger
      (test_auth_database TestLoadKey::test_permission_error_raises, test_cover_resolver
       TestSaveImage::test_os_error_returns_none, test_utilities_ops_hashing_extended checksum)
  - 1 unrelated env issue (test_upgrade_data_migration_dispatch, retry_count column)

CONCLUSION: dropping ffmpeg from CI is REJECTED, and the reason is worse than '3 tests fail'. FileNotFoundError subclasses OSError, and 8 of the 9 call sites catch OSError or bare Exception — so without ffmpeg those paths SILENTLY take their error branch. CI would look green while testing materially less. Only scanner/metadata_utils.py:run_ffprobe propagates.

--no-install-recommends VERIFIED SAFE: measured 306 pkgs/211.3MB -> 207 pkgs/135.8MB in clean ubuntu:24.04, and in debian:trixie-slim libopus/opus/libvorbis encoders + webm muxer all survive; a real libopus/webm encode succeeds. No codec loss.

Remaining decision: apt caching vs prebuilt container image, with --no-install-recommends in either case.
close_reason:
Fixed and verified end-to-end on real GitHub runners (commit 10762d3a).

COLD run 31018964261: cache miss as expected; --no-install-recommends cut the real-runner install from 306 pkgs/95.5MB to 89 pkgs/64.2MB; cache saved (61.19 MiB, verified via gh cache list, NOT via the step status — the 3.13 leg logged 'Failed to save: another job may be creating this cache', which is the benign expected race between the 3 matrix legs sharing one key; exactly one leg wins and saves).

WARM rerun: 'Cache hit', restored 64.2MB at 47 MB/s in ~1.7s, then 'Need to get 0 B/64.2 MB of archives' — zero bytes from azure.archive.ubuntu.com.

Test fidelity unchanged: 5112 passed, 130 skipped in both runs, identical to the pre-change baseline. ffmpeg retained.

Job wall-clock for the 3.13 leg: 50m32s (stalled run) -> 5m07s (cold) -> 4m43s (warm).

title: test_auth_performance.py asserts wall-clock timings with no tolerance — flakes on loaded CI runners
description:
Found 2026-08-03 during the v8.4.1.0 release, where it blocked a Dependabot PR merge and briefly looked like a real incompatibility.

WHAT HAPPENED: PR #117 (actions/setup-python 6.3.0 -> 7.0.0) failed its Python 3.14 leg with 3 failures out of 5242 tests. All three were wall-clock assertions:
  test_user_creation_latency        p95 188.53ms  (assert < 100ms)
  test_notification_bulk_create     2.28s         (assert < 2.0s)
  test_session_cleanup_performance  115.19ms      (assert < 100ms)
5109 passed. The same tests pass consistently on main (3 consecutive green CI runs).

WHY IT IS A PROBLEM: a setup-python version bump cannot selectively slow down auth database operations — it would surface as import or interpreter errors. The failure was runner contention. But the signal it produced was "this dependency upgrade breaks Python 3.14", which is exactly the wrong conclusion, and it cost a release cycle to disprove.

These are bare timing assertions on a shared GitHub-hosted runner whose CPU is contended and unpredictable. There is no @pytest.mark.flaky, no retry, and no tolerance band. There are at least 6 such assertions:
  library/tests/test_auth_performance.py:78   p95_time < 0.1
  library/tests/test_auth_performance.py:111  p95_time < 0.02
  library/tests/test_auth_performance.py:147  p95_time < 0.05
  library/tests/test_auth_performance.py:281  elapsed  < 2.0
  library/tests/test_auth_performance.py:339  elapsed  < 0.1
  library/tests/test_auth_performance.py:392  elapsed  < 0.1
The 20ms threshold at line 111 is the most exposed — a single scheduler preemption exceeds it.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND NOISE: intermittent red trains maintainers to re-run rather than read. That is precisely the habit that lets a genuine regression through, and this repo already carries the scar (95 consecutive red commits dismissed as pre-existing, see ~/.claude/rules/incidents.md).

OPTIONS:
1. Mark them @pytest.mark.performance and deselect on CI, running them only locally or on a dedicated runner. Keeps the intent, removes the false signal.
2. Keep them on CI but widen thresholds substantially (5-10x) so they only catch order-of-magnitude regressions, which is what a shared runner can actually measure.
3. Use pytest-benchmark (already a declared plugin) with relative comparison against a stored baseline instead of absolute wall-clock limits.

Option 1 or 3 preferred. Option 2 preserves the flake at a lower rate rather than removing it.

title: Credential scan in security-checks.yml only inspects HEAD~1, missing earlier commits in a multi-commit push
description:
Found 2026-08-03 while fixing a false positive in the same step.

.github/workflows/security-checks.yml 'Check for hardcoded credentials' runs:
    git diff HEAD~1 -- . ':(exclude).beads/' | grep -iE "$PATTERN"

WHY THIS IS A GAP: a push containing N commits is scanned for only the tip commit. A credential introduced in commit 1 of a 3-commit push is never examined, and the step reports 'No hardcoded credentials found' — a check that cannot show failure for most of the pushed content. This session pushed 2- and 3-commit batches routinely, so the window is real rather than theoretical.

FIX: scan the actual push range. For push events GitHub provides github.event.before / github.event.after; use 'git diff $BEFORE..$AFTER' with a fallback to HEAD~1 when before is all-zeroes (new branch / force push / initial commit). Pass the values via env: rather than inline ${{ }} interpolation to avoid workflow injection.

ALSO WORTH REVISITING while in here: the pattern itself is naive — '(api.?key|password|token|secret).*=.*["'][a-zA-Z0-9]{16,}["']' matches any line where those words appear anywhere before a long quoted alphanumeric, which is what produced the .beads/ false positive. A dedicated scanner (gitleaks / trufflehog) would be both stricter and less noisy, and gitleaks is already referenced in ~/.claude/rules/security.md for non-org repos.

title: "Remember me" cannot last 10 years — browsers clamp cookies to 400 days, and the session is never renewed
description:
Users of The Library eventually get signed out despite ticking "stay logged in". Two independent causes, both in library/backend/api_modular/auth_shared.py.

CAUSE 1 — the 10-year cookie does not exist.
  SESSION_DURATION_REMEMBER = 10 * 365 * 24 * 60 * 60  # ~10 years (until sign-out)   (auth_shared.py:121)
That comment is unachievable in every current browser. Chromium and Firefox both clamp a stored cookie to a maximum 400 days regardless of Max-Age (RFC 6265bis behaviour; Chrome 104+, Firefox 108+).

MEASURED 2026-08-03, not assumed. A local HTTP server issued Set-Cookie with Max-Age=315360000 (3650 days); the cookie was loaded in headless Chromium and headless Firefox with throwaway profiles and the stored expiry read straight out of each engine's cookie DB (Chromium Cookies.expires_utc; Firefox moz_cookies.expiry, milliseconds in current FF). Both stored EXACTLY 400 days. So the real ceiling for 'remember me' today is 400 days, and the constant is misleading anyone who reads it.

CAUSE 2 — the session is never renewed, so 400 days is measured from LOGIN, not from last use.
set_session_cookie() is called only from login/registration/recovery paths — auth.py:263, auth.py:342, auth_webauthn.py:427, auth_recovery.py:479, auth_registration.py:710. Nothing re-issues the cookie on an ordinary authenticated request. A user who visits daily is signed out on exactly the same schedule as one who never returns.

FIX — rolling renewal, the same change just made in cachyos-sentinel (commit e8a138c, sentinel-dash/src/hooks.server.ts): when a request arrives with a valid session past half its life, re-issue the cookie. Regular use then never expires (each renewal also resets the browser's own 400-day storage clock), while an abandoned or stolen cookie still lapses. Implement it once in the auth middleware so every route inherits it, rather than at the five login call sites.

ALSO REVIEW (not yet verified, flagged from a bounded read):
- maintenance_scheduler.py:238 runs a 'cleanup of stale sessions and expired tokens'. If server-side session rows are purged on a schedule, that is a SECOND cutoff which may fire earlier than the cookie and would defeat rolling renewal on its own. Confirm what it deletes and on what criterion; rolling renewal must touch the server-side row too, not just the cookie.
- Whether SESSION_DURATION_DEFAULT = None (a session cookie, cleared on browser close) is the intended non-remember behaviour.

mTLS — RAISED AND REJECTED FOR THIS PROJECT. It was the answer for sentinel's single-operator LAN dashboard (tracked there as cachyos-sentinel-zqmp) because a client certificate lives in the browser's cert store, which 'clear browsing data' does not touch. It does NOT transfer to The Library: it needs a certificate provisioned per user per device, which is unworkable for end users of a public-facing site and would become the account-recovery problem instead. Do not add it here.

FOREVER IS NOT AVAILABLE either way — no cookie survives a user clearing browsing data, and none exceeds 400 days unrenewed. Rolling renewal is the honest maximum: indefinite for active users. If the constant stays at 10 years, at minimum correct the comment so it stops asserting something browsers will not honour.

title: CI: add concurrency groups to all workflows (superseded runs overlap; deploy can race)
description: None of the 6 workflows in .github/workflows/ declare a 'concurrency:' block. Rapid pushes therefore run overlapping full pipelines for the same ref, burning minutes and letting the SLOWEST run — not the newest — report last. For release/deploy workflows two runs can additionally race each other. Found 2026-07-27 while harvesting this project's workflows as the reference implementation for the house CI/CD template; the gap is here, not in the template.
design:
Add to each workflow:

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

CRITICAL: do NOT set cancel-in-progress: true on release.yml or any deploy/publish workflow — cancelling a half-finished publish leaves partial artifacts, which is worse than letting it finish. Use the concurrency group there WITHOUT cancel-in-progress. Canonical guidance: ~/.claude/templates/ci-cd-pipeline.md section 7.
acceptance_criteria: Every workflow in .github/workflows/ has a concurrency block; release.yml and any deploy workflow have the group but NOT cancel-in-progress; a double-push to a branch shows the first run cancelled on CI but a tag push mid-release is not cancelled.

Polarity verified: cancel-in-progress true for the 3 read-only workflows (ci, python-security, security-checks), false for the 3 that publish/merge/commit (release, dependabot-auto-merge, security-autofix) — the issue named release.yml; extended to the other two for the same half-finished-mutation reason. Supersession proven live via throwaway PR #127 (closed, branch deleted): pushes a8dd0442 then f58f0e8c ~30s apart, push-1 CI and Python Security & Quality both reported 'cancelled'. Security Checks completed before the second push landed (correct, not a miss).

title: v8.4.1.0: Option B (gunicorn proxy) + Open Library print-pub-date enrichment
description:
Bundle two changes into the v8.4.1.0 minor release.

== Change 1: Option B — Gunicorn-ify audiobook-proxy ==

Replace `http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer` in `library/web-v2/proxy_server.py` with gunicorn workers (same engine as audiobook-api.service). Solves the latent concurrency bottleneck where 1-in-10 parallel requests can hit Caddy's dial_timeout under cold-state thundering-herd (e.g. post-upgrade, post-CF-cache-purge).

Scope:
- Refactor proxy_server.py into a WSGI app
- Update audiobook-proxy.service to ExecStart gunicorn (mirror audiobook-api.service pattern)
- Workers: probably 2-4 (lightweight proxy, not CPU-bound)
- Preserve all 5 functions: /api/* /auth/* /streaming-audio/* (forward) + /covers/* + web-v2/* (file_server)
- Preserve range request support for /streaming-audio/*
- Preserve CORS, CRLF validation, hop-by-hop header filtering
- Keep project self-contained (no Caddy-on-host dependency for other users)

Verification:
- Stress test: 100 parallel cover requests via Cloudflare, 0 failures
- Range-request smoke: seek mid-audio in player, verify HTTP 206 responses
- WebSocket smoke: /streaming-translate works for translation pipeline

Discovery context: 2026-05-23 prod upgrade to v8.4.0.1, post-upgrade visual verification surfaced transient 502s on cover load. Root cause = audiobook-proxy.service had just restarted, cold connection pool + thundering-herd. Steady-state confirmed clean (50/50 parallel succeed). Gunicorn fix prevents future transients under extreme load.

== Change 2: Open Library print-pub-date enrichment ==

Add a new column `audiobooks.original_publish_year` (keep `published_year` for back-compat). Backfill via Open Library lookups (ISBN/title → first_publish_year). Add UI sort option "Original Print Year" distinct from "Newest Released (Audio)" (v8.4.0.1) and "Newest Published (Book)" (current).

Scope:

- Fallback chain: Open Library → existing `published_year` if OL silent (~5% gap)
- UI: 3rd sort dimension; relabel for clarity (Print Year vs Audio Release)
- Curated zh-Hans translations
- Tutorial.js update

User context (2026-05-23):

This is a real data-quality improvement — the existing published_year is Audible-sourced and conflates book-pub-year with audiobook-release-year (~7.5% mismatches in prod DB).

== Why bundle ==

Both changes touch the serving/data layer. One release cycle for QA on test-VM, QA, Dev. Cleaner CHANGELOG narrative. No back-to-back micro-releases competing for QA time.

== Acceptance criteria ==

- 100-parallel cover load test: 0 failures (via Cloudflare)

- Backfill script populates original_publish_year for ≥90% of library

title: upgrade.sh::create_backup silently swallows cp failures
description: Why this issue exists: surfaced during v8.3.10.7 prod upgrade on 2026-05-12. The first attempt (sudo -u audiobooks ./upgrade.sh ...) failed at the backup step with 'Permission denied' because the audiobooks service account cannot write to /opt/ (only inside /opt/audiobooks/). The script printed the cp error but did NOT exit — it then echoed 'Backup created successfully' and continued. The retry as root succeeded but ALSO went through without ever recreating a fresh backup of the v8.3.10.6 state. Net result: prod upgraded to v8.3.10.7 with no on-disk backup of the previous version. Rollback is still possible from the GitHub v8.3.10.6 release tarball, but the locally-cached safety net was lost. What needs to be done: in upgrade.sh::create_backup (around line 528), check the cp exit code and abort the upgrade if backup creation failed. The script currently has no error checking after the cp command.
design:
Wrap both branches of the if-else with explicit exit:
```bash
if [[ -w "$target" ]]; then
    cp -a "$target" "$backup_dir" || { echo -e "${RED}Backup FAILED — aborting upgrade to preserve existing install${NC}"; exit 1; }
else
    sudo cp -a "$target" "$backup_dir" || { echo -e "${RED}Backup FAILED — aborting upgrade to preserve existing install${NC}"; exit 1; }
fi
echo -e "${GREEN}  Backup created successfully${NC}"
```
~5 lines. Pure additive — no behavior change on the success path.
acceptance_criteria: cp failure aborts upgrade with clear error message; success path unchanged; existing backup retention rolling-keep-5 logic untouched; manual test: simulate failure (e.g., chmod 000 /opt/) and confirm script exits non-zero before touching live install
notes: Surfaced during v8.3.10.7 prod upgrade. Per memory feedback_nopasswd_sudo_prod_deploys.md the documented prod-deploy command is `sudo -n -u audiobooks ./upgrade.sh ...` but that command silently doesn't back up because of this bug. Either fix the script (this issue) or update the memory to recommend `sudo -n ./upgrade.sh ...` as root, OR — better — fix the script AND keep the docs as-is so the documented command keeps working safely.
